title: The Law Commands, and Makes Us Know
description: The Law Commands, and Makes Us Know in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 121, headed “The law and gospel distinguished”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The law com-mands, and makes us know What du-ties to our God we owe; But 'tis the gos-pel must re-veal Where lies our strength to do his will.

lines: The law commands, and makes us know
What duties to our God we owe;
Where lies our strength to do his will.
The law discovers guilt and sin,
And shews how vile our hearts have been;
What curses doth the law denounce
Against the man that fails but once!
But in the gospel Christ appears
Pardoning the guilt of numerous years.
My soul, no more attempt to draw
Thy life and comfort from the law,
Fly to the hope the gospel gives;
The man that trusts the promise lives.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
